title: Perfect generators extend across an affine-open cover
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme], let U be a quasi-compact open subscheme and V an affine open subscheme with X = U union V. If P is a perfect generator of D_QCoh(O_U) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex, def-pc-generators], then there are a perfect object Q of D(O_X) whose restriction to U has P as a direct summand, and a perfect object K' of D(O_X) supported on the closed subset V minus U (meaning every cohomology sheaf vanishes on its complement), such that the direct sum Q $\oplus$ K' is a generator of D_QCoh(O_X).

source.place: Tag 09IS, proof (using Tags 09IQ and 09IR), induction step

proof.text: Apply the supported perfect-map lifting statement [lem-sc-perfect-support-map-lift] with T=X, E=0 and the zero map from P. Its hypotheses hold because X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, U is quasi-compact, and X minus T is empty. It produces a perfect Q on X whose restriction to U has P as a direct summand.

Write V=Spec(A) and Z=V minus U. Since U intersection V is quasi-compact, Z is the vanishing locus V(f_1,...,f_r) for finitely many f_i in A. Let K be the Koszul complex on the f_i over A. It is perfect, its cohomology is supported on Z, and the supported-open pushforward statement [lem-pc-supported-open-pushforward] makes K' = R(V \to X)_*K perfect on X and identifies K' with the extension-by-zero pushforward of K.

source.place: Tag 09IS, induction step, using Tags 09IQ and 09IR; Tag 08DP

proof.text: Let E be in D_QCoh(O_X) and suppose every Hom((Q \oplus K')[n],E) is zero. By the supported-open pushforward statement [lem-pc-supported-open-pushforward] (with T=Z, closed in X and contained in V), K' is the extension-by-zero pushforward of K, so the adjunction between extension by zero and restriction identifies Hom(K'[n],E) with Hom(K[n],E restricted to V). The Koszul orthogonality criterion [lem-pc-perfect-generation-koszul-orthogonal] therefore gives that the canonical map E restricted to V \to R(U intersection V \to V)_*(E restricted to U intersection V) is an isomorphism. Let j:U \to X be the inclusion and F=Rj_*(E restricted to U), with canonical (unit) map E \to F. By [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open] (applied to j and the open V, and to the open U), F restricted to V is canonically R(U intersection V \to V)_*(E restricted to U intersection V) and F restricted to U is E restricted to U; under these identifications the restriction of E \to F to V is the isomorphism just obtained and its restriction to U is the identity. A morphism in D(O_X) that is an isomorphism on each member of an open cover is an isomorphism (its cone has cohomology sheaves vanishing on each member, hence zero), so E \to F=Rj_*(E restricted to U) is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09IS, induction step, paragraph beginning Let E be an object

proof.text: Since E is R(U \to X)_*(E restricted to U), adjunction gives Hom(Q[n],E)=Hom(Q restricted to U[n],E restricted to U). The direct-summand decomposition of Q restricted to U contains Hom(P[n],E restricted to U) as a direct summand, so these groups vanish. Because P is a generator, E restricted to U is zero. Applying the already-proved isomorphism E=R(U \to X)_*(E restricted to U) gives E=0, so the direct sum Q \oplus K' is a generator.
